notes: The base revision is visible only through the unified diff; claims about base cite the hunks it contains and nothing beyond them.
The API delta reports no change to any kvstore public item other than evict_oldest, evict and capacity (72 unchanged), and no package version changes were recorded in the structural diff.

claims.text: Cache exposed `evict_oldest(&mut self, n: usize)`, documented as evicting the `n` oldest entries, but its loop was written `for _ in 0..=n`, an inclusive range, so it attempted n+1 removals rather than n.

The method returned nothing, so a caller had no way to learn how many entries were actually removed; the `if let Some(oldest)` simply skipped iterations once the order queue ran dry instead of stopping.
Cache::put computed `overflow = self.map.len() - self.max_entries` and called `self.evict_oldest(overflow + 1)`.
There was no public accessor for the cache's configured maximum; `free_slots` was the only method reading `max_entries` for callers, and it reported remaining space rather than the bound itself.

citations.item: pub fn kvstore::cache::Cache::evict(&mut self, usize) -> usize

claims.text: `evict(&mut self, n: usize) -> usize` loops `for _ in 0..n`, counts each entry it pops from `order` and removes from `map`, and returns that count; its doc comment now says "returning how many were removed".
The `if let` became a `match` whose `None` arm breaks out of the loop, so eviction stops as soon as the order queue is empty rather than continuing to spin through the remaining iterations.
Cache::put keeps the same `overflow + 1` argument but now calls `evict`, and discards the returned count.
A new `capacity(&self) -> usize` returns `max_entries` directly, documented as "The configured maximum number of entries."

Removing the public `evict_oldest` method is classified by the `inherent_method_missing` lint at major level, making the required version bump for the kvstore crate major; 72 other public items are unchanged.
kvstore/src/cache.rs no longer contains `evict_oldest`; it now contains `evict` and `capacity` instead.
The call edge from Cache::put to evict_oldest was removed and a call edge from Cache::put to evict added, which is the only call site of the renamed method in the graph.
The structural diff treats this as a likely rename rather than an unrelated add/remove pair: `evict_oldest` → `evict` in the same file with an overlapping source range, confidence 0.75.
Cache::put's own source range was edited but the symbol itself was neither added nor removed; it is reported as touched, along with the enclosing `cache` module.
handle_request reaches the changed code through Cache::put and could be affected; it is the single impacted symbol found at one hop, and it is on the public API surface.
This is bounded reverse reachability over calls and imports, so the entry is a possibility rather than a known breakage; published precision for this class of analysis is roughly 38-50%.
The kvstore-cli package was skipped by the API check because it has no library target to expose an API at either revision, so any use of evict_oldest there is not covered by the API delta.

Eviction count changed silently for every existing caller: the same argument `n` now removes at most n entries where it previously attempted n+1, so Cache::put, which still passes `overflow + 1`, evicts one fewer entry per overflow than before. Whether `overflow + 1` is still the right argument is the main thing to check.

Cache::put's overflow branch triggers on `self.map.len() >= self.max_entries`, so at exactly the bound `overflow` is 0 and one entry is evicted before the insert; the new early `break` means that when `order` is shorter than `map` the eviction can now remove fewer entries than requested and the map can stay over `max_entries`.
The new return value is the only signal that eviction fell short, and Cache::put ignores it, so a short eviction is not detectable at that call site.

put pushes the key onto `order` on every call without checking whether it already exists in `map`, so repeated puts of the same key grow `order` beyond `map.len()` — the condition under which the new `break` path is reached.

citations.item: pub fn kvstore::cache::Cache::evict(&mut self, usize) -> usize

claims.text: This is a breaking API change requiring a major bump: any external caller of `Cache::evict_oldest` must be updated to `Cache::evict`, and the crate's version was not changed as part of this diff.
`capacity` and the pre-existing `free_slots` now both read `max_entries` and are easy to confuse: `capacity` returns the configured bound, `free_slots` returns the bound minus the current length.

output.summary: Cache::evict_oldest is replaced by Cache::evict, which takes the same `n` argument but returns how many entries it actually removed, and a new Cache::capacity accessor exposes the configured maximum. The old method's loop ran `0..=n`, removing one entry more than asked for; the new one runs `0..n` and stops early when the order queue is empty. Cache::put is rewired to the new method, so the number of entries evicted on overflow drops by one per call. cargo-semver-checks flags the removal of the public evict_oldest as a major, breaking change for the kvstore crate.
